confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches that returned aggregated Faro price data (Numbeo-style crowd-sourced figures via Expatica and similar) plus travel-budget guides. Those showed an inexpensive meal of about EUR 12-13, a three-course mid-range dinner for two of about EUR 38-40, a cappuccino of about EUR 1.7-1.9 and a domestic draught beer of about EUR 2.5-3.1. I nudged these up slightly for July peak season and restaurant pricing. The cocktail anchor is less certain: guides gave EUR 7-10 and one dataset gave EUR 8. The wine-glass anchor is also less certain: guides gave about EUR 3-4 for house wine. Both were cross-checked against the local beer price relationship. EUR prices were converted to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.17 USD per EUR, which I did not verify by search. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season from general knowledge and the supplied context. I did not inspect any live listings or booking pages, so treat them as roughly +/-25%. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation my search surfaced (18 Nov 2026); no 19 Nov figure had appeared.
comparable_city_reasoning: Faro-specific aggregated price data was used directly for food and drink. Accommodation is modelled on July peak-season rates for mid-sized Algarve and southern Portugal cities, somewhat below beach-resort towns such as Lagos or Albufeira and below Lisbon.
